name: What if my existing garage has low ceilings for an in-law suite conversion?

mainEntity.name: What if my existing garage has low ceilings for an in-law suite conversion?
mainEntity.text: What if my existing garage has low ceilings for an in-law suite conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low ceiling height can be a major obstacle in a garage conversion because it affects comfort, code compliance, and the overall feel of the room. If the ceiling is too low, the project may require structural changes such as roof modification or slab adjustment, which can raise costs quickly. In some cases, another solution like an attached addition or interior conversion may be more practical. Before spending money on plans, homeowners should verify clear heights, slab conditions, and any obstructions such as ducting or framing. A good feasibility review can save time by identifying early whether the garage is a good candidate or whether another route will deliver a better result.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low ceilings can make a garage conversion harder because the space may not meet habitability or code expectations without structural changes. Depending on the situation, the solution may involve lowering the floor, raising the roof, or choosing a different type of suite. Ceiling height should be checked before design work begins.
